newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan to develop anti-missile missile - paper.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan to develop anti-missile missile - paper.

text.p: Taiwan will develop an anti- missile missile to bolster its defences against rival China, a newspaper run by the ruling Nationalist Party said on Thursday.

Preparatory work on the Sky Bow III system has begun at the military's Chung Shan Institution of Science and Technology, the Central Daily News quoted a high-level source at the weapons centre as saying.
The institute will also begin mass production soon of the home-grown Sky Bow II following successful tests of the ground- to-air missile at a military base at southern Pingtung, the paper said.
The defence ministry declined to comment on the report.
The Sky Bow missiles, along with the commissioning of U.S. Patriot anti-missile missiles and the deployment of U.S. F-16 fighters,
French Mirages and Taiwan's own Indigenous Defence Fighter aim to beef up Taiwan's defences in the face of rival China's military modernisation.

The first two F-16s were scheduled to arrive in Taiwan on April 15, the same day Taiwan forms its first Indigenous Defence Fighter squadron at the air force's Chingchuankang base in central Taiwan, military sources said.
Taiwan has ordered 150 F-16s from the United States.
Washington reserves a right to arm the island despite having diplomatic ties with China, which bitterly opposes such sales. The F-16s will be based in southern Chiayi and eastern Hualien.
The Nationalist-ruled island is building 130 of its own fighters for the air force to be deployed at Taichung in central Taiwan and Tainan in the south, military sources said.
An order of 60 Mirage 2000-5 fighters will be deployed in Hsinchu in northern Taiwan, officials said.

Taiwan began procuring advanced weapons and developing its own after the United States and other allies switched ties to Beijing, which regards Taiwan as a renegade province that must be brought under communist sovereignty.

Taiwan and China have been rivals since a civil war split them in 1949. China has vowed to attack the island if it strays from its course of eventual reunification with the mainland and opts for independence.
